content.value_statement: Building Git-compatible services is complex and easy to implement inconsistently. This skill provides gitoxide patterns for repository objects, packfiles, refs, and smart HTTP handlers.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to open or create bare repositories with gitoxide.
Provides patterns for reading and writing Git objects.
Demonstrates commit construction with tree, parent, message, and signature data.
Outlines smart HTTP upload-pack and receive-pack route handling.
Explains packfile generation from requested and existing object IDs.
Shows reference listing, atomic updates, and HEAD lookup patterns.
limitations: The examples are implementation patterns, not a complete production server.
Authentication, authorization, and request size limits are not fully specified.
The skill does not include tests, build files, or runnable sample projects.
Users need Rust, Git internals, and gitoxide familiarity.

use_cases.title: Build Git-Compatible Storage
use_cases.description: Use the patterns to design repository storage that reads objects, writes blobs, and creates commits.

use_cases.title: Add Smart HTTP Endpoints
use_cases.description: Map Git upload-pack and receive-pack flows into service routes with clear request parsing steps.

use_cases.title: Review Git Data Flow
use_cases.description: Use the examples to understand how refs, packfiles, commits, and object IDs connect.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Repository Pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of the skill concepts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the git-protocol skill to explain how gitoxide opens repositories and stores objects. Keep the explanation practical.

prompt_templates.title: Design Object Operations
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the git-protocol skill to outline object read, blob write, and commit creation steps for my Rust service.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Smart HTTP Routes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the git-protocol skill to design upload-pack, receive-pack, and info/refs handlers for an Axum service.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Git Backend Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the git-protocol skill to review my Git backend design for packfile generation, ref updates, and permission checks.

output_examples.input: Explain how to add object storage to a Rust Git service.
output_examples.output: A concise plan covering repository initialization, object lookup, blob writes, commit construction, and error handling points.

output_examples.input: Plan smart HTTP support for clone and push operations.
output_examples.output: A route-level design for upload-pack, receive-pack, info/refs, request parsing, packfile generation, and permission checks.
A checklist covering atomic ref updates, expected old object IDs, reflog messages, and HEAD resolution behavior.

best_practices: Validate repository owners, names, object IDs, and ref names before filesystem access.
Check permissions before accepting push data or updating refs.
Use atomic ref updates when replacing existing references.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the snippets as complete production-ready security controls.
Do not accept unbounded packfile uploads without size and object validation.
Do not update refs without comparing the expected previous object ID.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps design Rust Git repository operations using gitoxide patterns for objects, commits, packfiles, refs, and smart HTTP.

faq.question: Does it provide a complete Git server?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and examples that need production hardening, tests, and integration code.

faq.question: Which AI coding tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it execute Git commands?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed file is Markdown with Rust examples and gitoxide crate references.

faq.question: What should I secure before deployment?
faq.answer: Secure repository path handling, authentication, push authorization, request limits, object validation, and atomic ref updates.

faq.question: Is gitoxide required?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples and terminology are centered on the gitoxide Rust crate family.
